[[File:Johann Gottlob Friedrich Bohnenberger-3.jpg|thumb|Johann Gottlieb Friedrich von Bohnenberger.]]  
'''Johann Gottlieb Friedrich von Bohnenberger''' (5 June 1765 &ndash; 19 April 1831) was a German astronomer born at [[Simmozheim]], [[Duchy of Württemberg|Württemberg]].  He studied at the [[University of Tübingen]].   In 1798, he was appointed  professor of [[mathematics]] and [[astronomy]] at the university.

He published:  
* ''Anleitung zur geographischen Ortsbestimmung'' (Guide to geographic locations), 1795
* ''Astronomie'' (Astronomy), 1811
* ''Anfangsgründe der höhern Analysis'' (Initial reasons of higher analysis), 1812.

In 1817, he systematically explained the design and use of a [[gyroscope]] apparatus which he called simply a “Machine.” Several examples of the 'Machine' were constructed by [[Johann Wilhelm Gottlob Buzengeiger]] of Tübingen.  Johann 
Friedrich Benzenberg had already mentioned Bohnenberger's invention (describing it at length) in several letters beginning in 1810.<ref name="Wag-Trier2010">{{cite web |author1=Wagner, Jörg Friedrich and Andor Trierenberg |title=The Origin of the Gyroscope: The Machine of Bohnenberger |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259850564 |accessdate=18 October 2018 |date=December 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Wagner|first=Jörg F.|chapter=The Machine of Bohnenberger|date=2014|chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-39905-3_6|title=The History of Theoretical, Material and Computational Mechanics - Mathematics Meets Mechanics and Engineering|pages=81–100|editor-last=Stein|editor-first=Erwin|series=Lecture Notes in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics|place=Berlin, Heidelberg|publisher=Springer|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-39905-3_6|isbn=978-3-642-39905-3|access-date=2021-02-20|last2=Trierenberg|first2=Andor|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Bohnenberger died at [[Tübingen]].

The [[lunar crater]] [[Bohnenberger (crater)|Bohnenberger]] is named after him.
